BiblicalUsage: Nakal means to act treacherously, to defraud or deal subtilly, and it is used for brothers, for priests, and for whole peoples. In Genesis 37:18 Joseph's brothers conspire against him before he comes near to them, and in Numbers 25:18 the Midianites vex Israel with their wiles in the matter of Peor. In Psalm 105:25 God turns the Egyptians' hearts to deal subtilly with His servants, and in Malachi 1:14 cursed is the deceiver who has a male in his flock and vows and sacrifices a corrupt thing.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe treachery is the sin that hides behind a smile, because the brothers waited until Joseph was close, and the deceiver brings a corrupt thing to the altar with a vow on his lips. God sees the wiles, and the curse in Malachi 1:14 falls on the one who thought no one was watching. I hold that plain dealing is the only safe dealing.
